scenes.vo: Monday, the sixteenth of November, 2026. Five forty in the morning. Ransomware spreads through StonaWave, a drugmaker that supplies cancer treatments to hospitals in Europe and America. This is Operation Cold Chain.
scenes.title: COLD CHAIN
scenes.subtitle: The StonaWave ransomware crisis

scenes.vo: It began nineteen days earlier, with a contractor V P N account and no multi-factor authentication. A weak service account gave PharmLeaks the whole domain. For ten nights, patient and trial data slipped out. Then the backups were sabotaged.
scenes.heading: Nineteen days inside.

nodes.title: Contractor VPN access
nodes.sub: Bought from a broker, no MFA

nodes.title: Recovery sabotaged
nodes.sub: EDR off on 40 servers, backup catalogs deleted

nodes.title: Encryption
nodes.sub: Pushed by group policy to ERP, MES and identity

scenes.vo: At eight thirty, the crisis cell meets in Paris. Frankfurt has stopped two oncology lines. The Lyon warehouse is blind on temperatures, and hospitals cannot order. Only Hyderabad and its backup vault look untouched.
scenes.heading: One domain. Every site exposed.

scenes.vo: PharmLeaks writes to the executives: eighteen million dollars in seventy-two hours, or the data goes public. A broker already sells it on a dark web forum. Paying would not protect a single patient.
scenes.heading: Three crises. One clock.

facts.sub: the same data on sale on a dark web forum

scenes.vo: At ten, two thousand patient records appear online. CNN goes live, the press follows in three languages. CERT-FR, the CNIL and the health regulator each start a clock, and patients ask if their treatment will come.
scenes.eyebrow: Act II · 10:00 · The leak goes public
scenes.heading: Every audience adds a deadline

bottom.strong: The leak made it a patient crisis.

scenes.vo: The committee isolates every site and refuses to pay. Critical treatments leave Lyon on paper, temperatures logged by hand. At eleven, the Hyderabad vault is confirmed clean: the rebuild starts in a clean room.
scenes.eyebrow: Act III · Patients first, then recovery
scenes.heading: Rebuild on what can be trusted
scenes.strip:
Isolated sites · clean vault
clean-room rebuild · paper cold chain
scenes.footer: Recovery is a chain of trusted decisions.

scenes.vo: Three lessons. A contractor account without multi-factor authentication opened the door. Backups only count if the attacker cannot reach them. And in a drug company, every cyber decision is a patient decision.
scenes.eyebrow: What this means for the executive committee

lessons.text: Enforce MFA on every contractor and third-party access.
Keep one backup offline, tested and out of the domain's reach.
Weigh every cyber decision against patient safety.

scenes.finalLine1: The attackers came for the data.
scenes.finalLine2: The crisis was about the patients.
